players.product: High-complexity multilayer PCBs, substrates and advanced packaging for AI data-center/networking systems

quarterly_data.signal: Record Q3 (CEO Edwin Roks, CFO Dan Boehle): net sales of $1.2 billion versus $753 million in Q3 2025, up 60% year over year on growth across all end markets, most notably Data Center & Networking driven by AI; non-GAAP EPS of $1.46 per diluted share, a 118% improvement year on year (versus $0.67) - both above guidance and both all-time quarterly highs. Adjusted EBITDA was $242.3 million, a record 20.1% margin, up 400 basis points year over year and over 350 basis points sequentially on positive mix and operational execution. Non-GAAP gross margin was 24.8% versus 21.5% a year ago on volume and favourable Data Center & Networking and Aerospace & Defense mix plus execution improvements at Penang; non-GAAP operating margin was 17.4% versus 12.3%. GAAP operating income was $162.3 million (versus $71.9 million) and GAAP net income $84.8 million or $0.79 per diluted share; non-GAAP net income was $157.8 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 sales $1.2 billion (+60% YoY); non-GAAP EPS $1.46 (+118%); adjusted EBITDA $242.3 million (20.1%, +400 bps YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance raised and first 2027 outlook (CFO Dan Boehle): Q4 2026 net sales of $1.42 billion-$1.44 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.77-$1.83 per diluted share; full-year 2026 sales raised to approximately $4.47 billion-$4.49 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $4.97-$5.03. Preliminary full-year 2027 net sales of approximately $6.5 billion-$6.75 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $8.10-$8.90 on 108.1 million diluted shares. All ranges include recently closed acquisitions and their financing and exclude any pending acquisitions. CEO Edwin Roks: this year is about 48% growth 'and again, next year we will grow 50%', with 'a substantial part of that growth' from N+M while every end market grows; 'we are confident with the numbers we predicted for 2027'. CFO: as N+M becomes more of the mix, gross and EBITDA margins 'will be increasing more than 200 basis points in the next year.' End-market split for 2027 is to be given on the next call.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 2026 sales $1.42 billion-$1.44 billion, EPS $1.77-$1.83; FY2026 $4.47 billion-$4.49 billion, EPS $4.97-$5.03; FY2027 ~$6.5 billion-$6.75 billion, EPS $8.10-$8.90

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2026 modelling assumptions (CFO Dan Boehle): diluted share count of approximately 107.8 million (full-year 2026: 107.5 million), SG&A about 6.7% of net sales, R&D about 1% of net sales, interest expense of approximately $33.9 million, interest income of approximately $3.0 million and an effective tax rate between 15% and 19%. The CFO said two businesses that have closed or are expected to close around the end of Q3 into Q4 add to EBITDA in the Q4 guide, but higher interest expense of 'about $20 million a quarter' from the acquisition debt offsets part of that in EPS. On M&A, the CFO said 'this will be the end of the big stuff for a while'; TTM will focus on getting leverage back down, with positive free cash flow next year funding capital expenditures.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4: ~107.8 million diluted shares; SG&A ~6.7% of sales; interest expense ~$33.9 million; tax rate 15%-19%; interest expense up about $20 million a quarter

quarterly_data.signal: Orders at record levels (CEO Edwin Roks): overall book-to-bill was 2.1 in Q3, with the commercial reporting segment at 2.5 and the A&D reporting segment at 1.6. The 90-day backlog, subject to cancellations, was $1.3 billion versus $610 million a year ago, a 111% increase. Aerospace & Defense total program backlog reached a record $2 billion, up from just under $1.5 billion a year ago, with proposal activity at all-time highs; TTM already has visibility into roughly 65% of its projected A&D revenue for 2027. Q3 A&D bookings included the Surface Ship Surveillance, SPY-6 radar and APS-143 maritime surveillance radar programs, Golden Dome and a number of protected priority restricted programs, with new business from new primes.
quarterly_data.figure: Book-to-bill 2.1 (commercial 2.5, A&D 1.6); 90-day backlog $1.3 billion (+111% YoY); A&D program backlog $2 billion; ~65% of 2027 A&D revenue visible

quarterly_data.signal: Data Center & Networking was 41% of Q3 sales and grew 115% year over year on the strong ramp of TTM's N+M asymmetrical printed circuit boards and continued customer demand; it is guided to approximately 49% of Q4 net sales, and full-year 2026 sales in this end market are still expected to more than double. CEO Edwin Roks: the majority of this business is with 'industry-leading, innovative, established, and critical AI players'. Asked why the end market came in below the prior Q3 guide, the CEO said it was project timing on the customer side - 'there are no technical issues. Ramp is going well. Yield numbers are where they should be' - adding that customers have multiple suppliers and everybody 'has to be in that same window technology-wise', which 'sometimes hurting us also a bit'.
quarterly_data.figure: Data Center & Networking 41% of Q3 sales, +115% YoY; ~49% of Q4 sales; FY2026 more than double

quarterly_data.signal: N+M ramp (CEO Edwin Roks): N+M is currently about 30% of Data Center & Networking activity and will grow to about 50% of that group next year. Of three major N+M programs, two are doing really well and one moved 'a bit to the right' on that customer's program schedule, 'nothing to do' with technical issues or TTM's performance; the third program will ramp in the second half of Q4 and be fully in production in Q1. More N+M programs are coming ('the 5-10 programs all around'), with some pull-forward into Q3. For Q4 the CEO expects about the same N+M percentage, 'about 30% out of, let's say, a $700 million Data Center & Networking forecast' (later in the call: 'about 32% of the $670 million' in DCN, as spoken). N+M ASPs grow faster than cost as board complexity rises - 'about a factor of four' in value versus conventional architectures - and CFO Dan Boehle said the N+M gross margin is 'significantly higher than our corporate average.'
quarterly_data.figure: N+M ~30% of DC&N (Q3 and Q4), ~50% in 2027; Q4 DC&N forecast about $700 million; third program fully in production in Q1

quarterly_data.signal: Laminate and glass supply (CEO Edwin Roks, asked about CCL and T-glass): lead times are 'in the order of 12 weeks, sometimes a bit longer, sometimes 24 weeks, sometimes even a bit longer, depending on the materials. So far, I think we are handling this very well.' A&D supply is solid; on the Data Center & Networking side it is 'an ongoing activity' - lead times are going up, but bigger programs give more visibility. Material costs are going up and TTM is transparent with customers: 'the customers will take these price increases', helped by the higher N+M ASPs.
quarterly_data.figure: material lead times ~12 weeks, sometimes 24 weeks or longer

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity investment (CEO Edwin Roks): TTM has invested or committed to invest over $1.3 billion in capacity expansion in the 2025 to 2029 timeframe across Data Center & Networking and Aerospace & Defense. The additional $400 million planned investment announced last week is expected to begin in Q4 2026 and continue into early 2028, primarily supporting revenue production in 2028; the CEO called it 'pure N+M, rounding numbers here', on top of the $1.2 billion multi-year expansion through 2029, done brownfield in buildings close to existing plants with 'a lot of equipment' to grow N+M. Management expects to fund these investments from operating cash without anticipated need to access its borrowing facilities. TTM is in the early stages of investing in a new innovation center in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, near its Chippewa Falls technology center, to spearhead R&D on mSAP, SAP, passives and advanced optics. CFO Dan Boehle: Penang is still expected to approach breakeven in Q4 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: over $1.3 billion committed 2025-2029; $400 million from Q4 2026 into early 2028 for 2028 revenue (N+M)

quarterly_data.signal: Aerospace & Defense was 34% of Q3 sales and grew 21% year over year on defense budget tailwinds, program alignment and bookings for new and ongoing programs. It is guided to approximately 31% of Q4 sales with year-on-year and sequential growth, and full-year 2026 growth of approximately 20% compared to 2025, 'including contributions from acquired businesses of roughly 8% on organic basis' (as spoken). CEO Edwin Roks: about half of the A&D business is now 'up the chain' sensing and communication; A&D 'will do better and better' in 2027, citing munitions, Golden Dome and 'a lot of radar'.
quarterly_data.figure: A&D 34% of Q3 sales, +21% YoY; ~31% of Q4 sales; FY2026 ~20% growth

quarterly_data.signal: Medical, industrial and instrumentation was 18% of Q3 sales and grew 97% year over year, aided by price adjustments to capture the value of TTM's technology and by demand in instrumentation for automatic test equipment supporting AI solutions; it is guided to approximately 14% of Q4 sales, growing roughly 90%, and nearly 70% growth for full-year 2026. Automotive was 7% of Q3 sales, up 11%; guided to about 6% of Q4 sales with double-digit growth as materials-availability challenges are worked through, and full-year 2026 automotive sales are now expected to improve mid-single digits versus the prior expectation of a mid-single-digit decline. CEO Edwin Roks sees additional automotive share opportunities as some competitors reduce their market participation. On 2027, the CEO said all end markets are growing and, although Data Center & Networking grows so fast 'that it does not look like the others are growing', 'I can tell you it is growing over 20%'.
quarterly_data.figure: MI&I 18% of Q3 sales, +97% YoY, FY2026 nearly 70%; automotive 7% of Q3 sales, +11%

quarterly_data.signal: Acquisitions status (CEO Edwin Roks): the Swiss Technology Group AG acquisition has closed and is now called TTM GS Swiss; TTM believes it is nearing the close of ILFA; Epiq Solutions closed on September 30; and last week TTM engaged in plans to acquire two small printed circuit board companies under the Merlin PCB Group holding company in the U.K. The planned Ophir Optics acquisition would establish a presence in Israel and Romania; the CEO plans to combine Ophir's infrared optics with TTM's RF radar systems into small-form-factor mission subsystems for unmanned and counter-unmanned aerial systems, with Epiq adding processing, while in industrial Ophir provides laser optical subsystems for shaping laser beams in industrial cutting, welding and PCB drilling machines. The CEO said Ophir is 'over 85% booked' for 2027, is experiencing strong revenue growth and margin expansion, and is expected to be immediately accretive to adjusted EBITDA margins and non-GAAP EPS, with closing hoped for at the end of Q2 2027. All acquisitions together are 'about half a billion in sales' of the 2027 outlook.
quarterly_data.figure: Ophir over 85% booked for 2027; acquisitions about half a billion in 2027 sales
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: seller of the Ophir Optics business

quarterly_data.signal: Cash flow and other Q3 items (CFO Dan Boehle): cash flow from operating activities was $154.7 million (versus $141.8 million a year ago) and free cash flow $74.8 million (versus $42.6 million). R&D expense was $9.5 million, just under 1% of net sales. Interest expense was $12.1 million, and the effective tax rate was 19.5%, giving tax expense of $38.2 million. A realized foreign exchange loss of $4.1 million was driven by the weakening of the U.S. dollar.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 OCF $154.7 million; FCF $74.8 million; R&D $9.5 million
